name: Gravitational Instantons
description: Spaces of four dimensions with no time in them, the solutions of Einstein's equations with Riemannian signature that Stephen Hawking, Gary Gibbons, Don Page, and Christopher Pope found in 1977 and 1978. The first is Schwarzschild's black hole in imaginary time, which closes smoothly on its horizon only if that time is a circle of length $4\pi r_s$, the inverse of Hawking's temperature. The others are the two Taub-NUT instantons, the spaces with many centres, the complex projective plane, and Page's space.
convention: All four coordinates are spatial, so no component carries a factor of $c$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to arc length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history:
A black hole has a temperature, $T = \hbar c^3/8\pi GMk_B$, which Stephen Hawking found in 1974 by following quantum fields through the collapse of a star [hawking1974, hawking1975]. Three years later he and Gary Gibbons found the same temperature sitting in Schwarzschild's metric [gibbons1977action]. With the time written $t = -i	au/c$ the metric is $$ds^2 = \left(1 -  rac{r_s}{r}ight)d	au^2 + \left(1 -  rac{r_s}{r}ight)^{-1}dr^2 + r^2\left(d	heta^2 + \sin^2	heta\,d\phi^2ight),$$ four dimensions of space and no time, and near $r = r_s$ the part in $r$ and $	au$ is a sheet of polar graph paper with $	au$ for its angle [gibbonshawking1979]. The middle of such a sheet is a point like any other only if the angle closes after one turn, and here one turn is $4\pi r_s$ of $	au$, which is $8\pi GM/c^2$ [gibbonshawking1979]. A quantum field that repeats in imaginary time is a field in equilibrium at a temperature, and the period $4\pi r_s$ is $\hbar c/k_BT$ for Hawking's $T$ [gibbonshawking1979, gibbons1977action].¶Is a space with no time in it good for anything? Gibbons and Hawking put it to work: its action is finite, and from the action they computed an entropy "equal to one quarter the area of the event horizon in fundamental units" [gibbons1977action]. Hawking named the kind of space that same year, after the instantons of Yang-Mills theory, the solutions with finite action in four Euclidean dimensions that Alexander Belavin, Alexander Polyakov, Albert Schwarz, and Yu.S. Tyupkin had found in 1975 [bpst1975, hawking1977]. "By analogy with Yang-Mills' theory", he wrote, "gravitational instantons are defined to be solutions of the classical Einstein equations which are non-singular on some section of complexified spacetime and in which the curvature dies away at large distances" [hawking1977]. His two examples were the "Schwarzschild and Taub-NUT solutions", "the latter being self-dual" [hawking1977].¶The Taub-NUT instanton closes in another way [gibbonshawking1979]. Its circle of imaginary time, of period $8\pi n$, shrinks to nothing at $r = n$ together with the spheres around it, so the space closes on a single point, the origin of flat space in polar coordinates, where Schwarzschild's closes on a whole sphere [gibbonshawking1979]. Hawking had a version with many such points, and in 1978 he and Gibbons wrote the family as $$ds^2 = V^{-1}\left(d	au + \vec{\omega}\cdot d\mathbf{x}ight)^2 + V\,d\mathbf{x}\cdot d\mathbf{x}, \qquad V = \epsilon + \sum_i  rac{2n}{|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_i|},$$ with $
abla	imes\vec{\omega} = 
abla V$ [hawking1977, gibbonshawking1978, eguchigilkeyhanson1980]. With $\epsilon = 1$ and one centre this is the Taub-NUT instanton again, and with $\epsilon = 0$ and two centres it is Tohru Eguchi and Andrew Hanson's space [eguchigilkeyhanson1980, gibbonshawking1979]. A second Taub-NUT instanton came from Don Page the same year, with the mass $5n/4$ where Hawking's has $n$: "Unlike the first Taub-NUT instanton known, this example has an event horizon and is not self dual" [page1978bolt, eguchigilkeyhanson1980].¶Gibbons and Hawking's sorting of all these spaces, in their classification of 1979, goes by the places a symmetry leaves fixed: "isolated points which we call 'nuts' and 2-surfaces which we call 'bolts'" [gibbonshawking1979]. The nut is named "after the self-dual Taub-NUT solution" and the bolt "for obvious reasons", with Schwarzschild's horizon its "canonical example" [gibbonshawking1979]. Counting them gives the topology: "the Euler number is the sum of the number of nuts, the number of antinuts and twice the number of bolts", which makes $2$ for Schwarzschild's one bolt and $1$ for Taub-NUT's one nut [gibbonshawking1979]. The bolts carry the thermodynamics as well, "an intrinsic gravitational entropy equal to one quarter the sum of their areas" [gibbonshawking1979].¶Can a gravitational instanton close up on every side? With a positive cosmological constant it has to, since every such solution is compact [gibbonshawking1979]. The 4-sphere, de Sitter space in imaginary time, and the product of two 2-spheres were known, and in 1978 Gibbons and Christopher Pope added the complex projective plane with the metric "known to mathematicians as the Fubini-Study metric", $$ds^2 =  rac{dr^2}{\left(1 + \Lambda r^2/6ight)^2} +  rac{r^2\left(d\psi + \cos	heta\,d\phiight)^2}{4\left(1 + \Lambda r^2/6ight)^2} +  rac{r^2\left(d	heta^2 + \sin^2	heta\,d\phi^2ight)}{4\left(1 + \Lambda r^2/6ight)},$$ which has a nut at $r = 0$ and a bolt at infinity [gibbonspope1978, gibbonshawking1979]. They called it "a gravitational pseudoparticle surrounded by an event horizon", and recorded that it "has no Lorentzian section" and "no spinor structure" [gibbonspope1978]. Page found a fourth compact instanton the same year, a limit of the rotating black hole in de Sitter space continued to imaginary time, whose two bolts are both smooth only where $
u^4 + 4
u^3 - 6
u^2 + 12
u - 3 = 0$, at $
u = 0.2817$ [page1978compact, gibbonshawking1979, page2009]. It is "the nontrivial $S^2$ fibre bundle over $S^2$", the projective plane with its nut "blown up" into a second bolt [page1978compact, page2009].¶Page's talk in Moscow that December counted four compact instantons with a positive cosmological constant, three of them "long known to geometers", and called them "the only ones known" [page2009]. His own is conformal to a Kähler metric, and so is the Einstein metric that Xiuxiong Chen, Claude LeBrun, and Brian Weber proved to exist, thirty years on, on the projective plane blown up at two points [page2009, chenlebrunweber2008]. Of Schwarzschild's instanton and Kerr's, Gibbons and Hawking had written that "By the No Hair Theorems these are the only solutions which are asymptotically flat in the conventional sense" [gibbonshawking1979]. Yu Chen and Edward Teo's instanton of 2011 is a third, with Euler number $3$ and signature $1$, and with it they showed that the conjecture that Schwarzschild's and Kerr's are the only asymptotically flat instantons "is false" [chenteo2011].

related.text: Schwarzschild's black hole with its time made imaginary is the first of these instantons. The horizon becomes the bolt, and the period $4\pi r_s$ that makes the bolt smooth is the inverse of Hawking's temperature [gibbons1977action, gibbonshawking1979].

Taub-NUT with $t = -i\tau/c$ and $l = in$ is real again, and it is regular at two masses: $m = n$, Hawking's self dual instanton, and $m = 5n/4$, Page's instanton with a bolt [hawking1977, page1978bolt, gibbonshawking1979].
Gibbons and Hawking's metric of many centres, taken with two of them and no constant in its potential, $\epsilon = 0$, is the Eguchi-Hanson space [gibbonshawking1979, eguchigilkeyhanson1980].

Give the self dual Taub-NUT instanton a time of its own, $-c^2dt^2$, and it is a static vacuum of five dimensions that four dimensions see as a magnetic monopole. The nut parameter is $n = 2m$ in the monopole's units [sorkin1983, grossperry1983].

Page's space is a limit of the Kerr-de Sitter metric in imaginary time: the black hole's horizon and the cosmological one are brought together, and the space between them closes smoothly at one value of the spin [page1978compact, gibbonshawking1979].

De Sitter space in imaginary time is the 4-sphere of radius $\sqrt{3/\Lambda}$, the first compact gravitational instanton. Its cosmological horizon is a bolt, and a quarter of the bolt's area is the horizon's entropy [gibbonshawking1979, page2009].
Half of the four sphere, the instanton of de Sitter space, joined at its equator to the waist of de Sitter's closed universe as Vilenkin's universe created from nothing [vilenkin1982].

parameters.description: The Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$: the bolt $r = r_s$ is a 2-sphere of radius $r_s$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $\tau$ the imaginary time, $t = -i\tau/c$ in Schwarzschild's chart, a length of period $4\pi r_s$. The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$.

parameters.description: The Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$: the bolt $x = 0$ is a 2-sphere of radius $r_s$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\rho, z, \phi, \tau)$, with $\rho$, $z$, and $\phi$ cylindrical coordinates on a flat space of three dimensions, every centre on its axis at a height $z_i$, and $\tau$ a length of period $8\pi n$.
